state: Context for two I17 integration judgments. The K27 observer (service.ts, 844 lines; service-check.ts, 17 checks) is the last doubles family awaiting a merge: ObjectStoreService offers 15 candidate verbs — sharedDigest, openPrefix, receipt, closePrefix, openSession, sessionTokenForTest, closeSession, put, settleWrite, pending, get, delete, compareBytes, list, sealCleanup — while prefixCount/liveSessionCount remain host-side like prior getters. Its records are PrefixReceipt, SessionFacts, ObjectFacts, WriteFacts, PageFacts, PendingFacts, CleanupReceipt; its errors are ObjectStoreError instances over 20 fixed codes (unknown-prefix, prefix-closed, capacity-exhausted, wrong-owner, closed-handle, keys-remain, pending-writes, scan-incomplete, session-live, unknown-session, forged-token, forged-continuation, stale-continuation, unknown-key, key-escapes-prefix, malformed-key, write-unknown, write-busy, write-settled, bad-page) each bound to engine, driver, or store. The constructor pins (owner, prefix) grant pairs, a never-read foreign sharedKeys map (sharedBucket seeds 3 shared keys), and limits maxPrefixes/maxSessions/maxObjects/maxObjectBytes/maxPageSize/maxPendingWrites; pinned self-check fixtures are owner-a/tenant-a/owned, owner-b/tenant-b/owned, 3 shared keys, and roomyLimits 4/8/32/1024/8/16. Sessions authenticate by sess- hex lookup; listings advance by opaque single-use cont- continuations that go stale on mutation; put/get shuttle copied Uint8Arrays proven by digest; compareBytes returns bool but reports malformed-key for untyped operands. House rules from I13-I16: fresh db:: package + db::db_fault{layer, code} for doubles, owner-first verbs with row elision, NT-I admission tags, verbatim {layer, code} failures, wrappers pairing facts with tokens, bytes::buffer + option::value<str> crossings (I15), and void results where apt. The s3:: package (16 verbs + s3:: errors) is the live client; K27's scope statement bars the observer from sharing executable material with it. K27 stands ledger-complete (evidence status stale); I17 ships provisional until P14, claiming no execution credit.

i17_observer_package.instructions: Fourteen doubles-observer verbs need a catalogue home. One candidate extends the live s3:: client package; two mint a fresh package under different nouns. Considering contract legibility for generation-minded authors (explicit lanes, no live-vs-doubles ambiguity) and the I13 precedent of minting db:: for doubles, which home serves readers best?

criteria.new_store_package: New store:: package + store::store_fault{layer, code} for all 14 verbs as owner-first operations (open_prefix/receipt/close_prefix/open_session/close_session/put/settle_write/pending/get/delete/compare_bytes/list/seal_cleanup/shared_digest), void results preserved, bytes::buffer payloads, option::value<str> continuation. Readers see doubles verbs under store:: and live verbs under s3:: with no overlap; follows the I13 mint-a-package precedent exactly.
criteria.new_objects_package: New objects:: package + objects::object_fault{layer, code} for the same 14 owner-first verbs. Same doubles/live split as new_store_package, but the package noun echoes the object/key/digest record language instead of the service-class noun. The judgment is purely which noun reads better in generated Can.
criteria.extend_s3_package: Same 14 verbs land in s3:: with a new s3::observer_fault{layer, code}, avoiding a 46th package and a third fault family. Readers meet one object package, but must distinguish live verbs (presign, multipart upload) from doubles verbs (continuations, seal_cleanup) by memory rather than by lane, against K27's no-sharing scope.

i17_session_token_shape.instructions: Every effectful verb authenticates with the sess- token, yet openSession omits it from SessionFacts and only the test-only sessionTokenForTest discloses it. Should the adapter fuse disclosure into open_session (one wrapper, no new verb) or expose disclosure as its own verb? Weigh stable-surface economy and fidelity to the I13-16 wrappers against pass-through transparency and the honest visibility of test-only machinery.

criteria.compose_token_in_adapter: Fuse: adapter open_session internally sequences openSession + sessionTokenForTest and returns facts-with-token, reproducing the I13-16 wrapper silhouette with zero added verbs. The test-only readout runs on every open yet stays non-addressable; its behavior is covered by adapter contract tests and the port differential rather than by a catalogue operation.
criteria.expose_token_op: Expose: add a dedicated owner-first token verb that passes straight through to sessionTokenForTest, so each catalogue operation maps to exactly one service method and the test-only accessor remains explicit surface. Costs one verb and normalizes test-only access as a stable operation, but nothing is fused or hidden.
